hints.title: Linear Time Constant Space Voting Obstacle
hints.text: Sorting takes logarithmic factor time and frequency counting uses linear auxiliary space. Given that the target element appears strictly more than half the time, how can pairing distinct elements cancel them out without allocating extra space?

hints.title: Boyer-Moore Pairwise Cancellation
hints.text: Maintain a running candidate and a net balance score. Increment the score when encountering the candidate and decrement when encountering a different value; reset the candidate whenever balance reaches zero.

hints.title: Single Pass Voting Procedure
hints.text: Initialize candidate to None and count to zero. Loop through every element. If count is zero, set candidate to the current element. Add one to count if the element matches candidate, otherwise subtract one. Return candidate after finishing the loop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 5 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm in a single pass with O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A frequency hash map requires O(N) auxiliary space. Sorting takes O(N log N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boyer-Moore achieves O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space by pairwise cancellation of non-matching values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why the majority element is guaranteed to survive pairwise cancellation (frequency > N/2).
